Several places to go deeper than this lesson, or to check a citation yourself before it goes in a
real Lakeshore document. All were checked and loading at the time this page was written.

- **[21 CFR 211.68, Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/211.68)**
  — the regulatory floor this lesson's patch VIAs and periodic reviews both answer to, in Cornell's
  free, citable, plain-text CFR mirror. The same section module 1 quoted in full; useful here as a
  quick reference without pulling up the whole lesson again.

- **[FDA guidance page: Blood Establishment Computer System Validation in the User's Facility](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/blood-establishment-computer-system-validation-users-facility)**
  — the same guidance this course has quoted since module 1, the source for this lesson's section
  III.I ("Validation after a Change"), III.C, and III.G quotes. Worth reading section III.I in full
  once: this lesson quotes nearly all of it, but the surrounding paragraphs on vendor contracts and
  manufacturer notification are real context this lesson only names in passing.

- **[NIST SP 800-40 Revision 4, Guide to Enterprise Patch Management Planning](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/40/r4/final)**
  — a free, public NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology) publication on patch
  management as an enterprise IT discipline: classifying patches, prioritizing them, and testing
  before deployment. It isn't written for FDA-regulated systems and doesn't mention validation or
  regression analysis — read it as the general ITSM backdrop this lesson's "patch classes with
  pre-analyzed regression plans" idea sits on top of, not as a source for anything BECS-specific.

- **[Patch Management, explained](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0lo3sTdf4eA)** (Group-IB, from
  oEmbed `author_name`) — a short general-IT training explainer on the patch management cycle.
  Industry cybersecurity content, not regulator-authored, and not blood- or validation-specific;
  watch it for the ITSM vocabulary only. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).

- **AABB Standards, Section 3.9, "Information Systems"** — not independently link-verified this
  session (see `sources/aabb/information-systems-section-3.9.md` for how its section number and
  themes were cross-confirmed). AABB's accreditation-side counterpart to this lesson's
  validated-state discussion, notably backup/continuity and disaster recovery (3.9.2) and documented
  change processes, checked by an AABB assessor rather than an FDA investigator. Start from
  **[AABB: Standards for Blood Banks and Transfusion
  Services](https://www.aabb.org/standards-accreditation/standards/blood-banks-and-transfusion-services)**
  (verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11, HTTP 200) for the catalogue page; the full standard
  text sits behind AABB's member/purchase access, so the free page won't show Section 3.9's actual
  requirement language.

- **[NIST SP 800-128, Guide for Security-Focused Configuration Management of Information
  Systems](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/128/final)** — free NIST guidance on establishing a
  baseline configuration and controlling changes to it, the general-IT version of this lesson's
  configuration-drift check against the validated baseline. Security-focused and not written for
  FDA-regulated systems. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[ISPE: GAMP 5 Guide, 2nd Edition](https://ispe.org/publications/guidance-documents/gamp-5-guide-2nd-edition)**
  — the publisher's catalogue page for the industry guide behind this lesson's periodic-review
  concept (named and paraphrased here, never quoted; the guide itself is copyrighted and
  purchase-only, so the page describes it rather than reproducing it). Verified loading via `curl`
  on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[21 CFR 11.10, Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/11.10)**
  — the Part 11 controls for closed systems, including the validation requirement in 11.10(a) that
  the periodic review's "is it still validated" question rests on, in Cornell's free plain-text
  mirror. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about keeping a system validated through patches, change and periodic review.

- **[CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations Guide](https://destcert.com/resources/cissp-domain-7-security-operations/)** (Destination Certification, commercial CISSP training) — an overview of security operations including configuration, change and patch management. Supports **CISSP Domain 7 (Security Operations)**. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[CISSP Domain 7 Summary: Security Operations](https://www.cybernous.com/resources/domain-summaries/cissp-domain-7-summary-security-operations/)** (Cybernous, commercial study site) — a concise Domain 7 summary for a second pass. Also supports **CISSP Domain 7**. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Mastering Periodic Review in GxP Environments](https://www.usdm.com/resources/blogs/mastering-periodic-review-in-gxp-environments)** (USDM, life-science consultancy blog) — how organisations plan and run periodic reviews of validated systems. Vendor content; useful for practical structure. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Computerized System Change Control and Revalidation](https://usvalidation.com/kb_article/cs-change-control-revalidation/)** (US Validation, consultancy knowledge-base article) — explains how change control decides how much re-testing a change needs. Useful for the patch-or-not discussion. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
